I read the structure region by region, starting from the ester at the top.

**Chain from the ester:** MeO2C is attached to CH=CH, then CH2, then CH2, then a C≡C that joins the benzene ring. That gives the chain COC(=O)C=CCCC#C-Ar.

**Alkene geometry:** The drawing places MeO2C–C at the upper left, then C=C going down-right, then the chain continuing. The ester carbon is at (140, 40), the alkene carbon C2 at (190, 55), C3 at (240, 30)... Reading the image coordinates, the ester carbonyl carbon is at about (140, 40). C2 is at about (185, 60) and C3 at about (240, 30). C4 is at about (285, 60) and then C5 at about (285, 120), which is the alkyne start.

Taking the substituents on the double bond: C2 has the C(=O) substituent, which sits to the upper left of C2, and C3 has the CH2 (C4), which sits to the lower right of C3. The double bond runs from lower left to upper right. The C(=O) lies up and left of C2, and C4 lies down and right of C3, so they are on opposite sides of the bond. This is the trans (E) arrangement.

**Ring and second arm:** The benzene is ortho-disubstituted. The other substituent is C≡C–CH2–O–CH=CH2, a vinyl ether on a propargyl unit.

**SMILES:** The E alkene is written as COC(=O)/C=C/CCC#Cc1ccccc1C#CCOC=C.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/CCC#Cc1ccccc1C#CCOC=C
